seoTitle: How to Connect FedEx to Shopify with MultiParcels
metaDescription: Integrate your FedEx account with Shopify using the MultiParcels app — install it from the App Store, connect your shop, and add FedEx as a carrier.
intro: Shopify's built-in shipping doesn't include FedEx as a native carrier option on every plan, which is where a multi-carrier app like MultiParcels comes in — it sits between your store and carriers like FedEx, so rates, labels, and tracking all flow through one dashboard. This guide covers finding MultiParcels in the Shopify App Store, connecting your store to it, and where the FedEx account itself gets added once the app is installed.

steps.heading: Start from your Shopify admin
steps.body: Log into your Shopify admin and land on the Home dashboard, which shows recent session and sales analytics alongside the familiar left-hand menu — Orders, Products, Customers, Marketing, Discounts, Content, Markets, and Analytics, with Apps further down. This is also where any apps you've already installed show up in the sidebar, so it's a useful place to confirm you don't already have a conflicting shipping app running before adding another.

image.caption: The Shopify admin Home dashboard, with session and sales data plus the full navigation sidebar where installed apps also appear.

steps.heading: Search the Shopify App Store for MultiParcels
steps.body: From Apps, click to browse or search the Shopify App Store and type "fedex." The results page returns well over a hundred matches, including FedEx-specific apps like PH Ship Rate & Track for FedEx, general shipping platforms like ShipStation and Shippo, and MultiParcels Shipping & Labels — described as letting you save time with multi-carrier shipping, tracking, and more. MultiParcels is worth choosing specifically when you want one dashboard that can eventually handle more than just FedEx, rather than a single-carrier tool.

image.caption: Shopify App Store search results for "fedex," showing MultiParcels Shipping & Labels alongside other FedEx and multi-carrier shipping apps.

steps.heading: Install the app and connect your Shopify store
steps.body: After installing MultiParcels, it opens its own dashboard outside the Shopify admin. Under Integrations in the left sidebar, the Shops section is where your store connection lives — a My shops panel lists each connected store by its myshopify.com address, with Edit, Pickup locations, Disable, and a Check connection button to confirm the link is live. An Add new shop panel sits alongside it, listing platforms MultiParcels can connect to beyond Shopify, including WooCommerce, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Etsy, eBay, and Zyro, each with its own tutorial link.

image.caption: The MultiParcels dashboard's Shops page, showing a connected Shopify store with Edit, Pickup locations, and Disable options, plus other platforms you can add.

steps.heading: Add your FedEx account under Carriers
steps.body: Once your store is connected, the FedEx account itself gets added under Carriers — a separate menu item in the same Integrations section as Shops. This is where MultiParcels asks for your FedEx account details so it can pull live rates and generate labels using your negotiated pricing rather than generic public rates. Keep your Shops and Carriers connections separate in your head: Shops is your storefront, Carriers is who actually ships the package.

steps.heading: Configure which FedEx services show at checkout
steps.body: With FedEx connected as a carrier, go into your shipping settings inside MultiParcels to choose which specific FedEx services — standard ground, express, international, and so on — you want customers to see as options at checkout. Narrowing this list to what you actually use keeps checkout simple for customers instead of overwhelming them with every FedEx service tier that exists.

steps.heading: Generate labels from incoming orders
steps.body: Once an order comes in on Shopify, it flows through to MultiParcels' Orders and Shipments sections, where you can generate a FedEx shipping label directly rather than logging into a separate FedEx portal. Automations in MultiParcels can also apply rules to new orders, which is useful once your shipping volume grows past manually processing each one by hand.

steps.heading: Confirm fulfillment updates flow back to Shopify
steps.body: After a label is created and a package ships, check that the order status and tracking number sync back to the original order in Shopify — this is the whole point of routing FedEx through an app rather than handling it separately, since customers should see accurate tracking without you updating two systems manually.

faq.question: Do I need an existing FedEx account?
faq.answer: Yes. MultiParcels connects to a FedEx account you already have under its Carriers section — it doesn't create a new FedEx business account for you.

faq.question: Is MultiParcels free to use?
faq.answer: It's free to install from the Shopify App Store, though shipping apps like this typically have paid tiers for higher volume — check the current plan details on the app's listing before relying on it at scale.

faq.question: Can I use multiple carriers alongside FedEx in MultiParcels?
faq.answer: Yes. Carriers and Shops are separate sections in the MultiParcels dashboard, so you can connect FedEx plus other carriers, and even connect stores from other platforms like WooCommerce or Etsy alongside Shopify.

faq.question: Will shipping labels print automatically for new orders?
faq.answer: Labels aren't generated automatically by default — you typically create them from the Orders or Shipments section in MultiParcels, though its Automations feature can apply rules to speed this up for high order volumes.

faq.question: Where do I check if my Shopify store is properly connected to MultiParcels?
faq.answer: On the Shops page under Integrations in the MultiParcels dashboard, your store is listed with a Check connection button that confirms the link between your Shopify store and MultiParcels is active.
